title: Real-Time Hybrid Optimization Models for Edge-Based Financial Risk Assessment: Integrating Deep Learning with Adaptive Regression for Low-Latency Decision Making
authors: Ahmed, M. P.; Tisha, S. A.; Sweet, M. M. R.
venue: Journal of Business and Management Studies
tldr: A hybrid optimization framework combining deep neural networks with adaptive regression reduces edge inference latency by up to 55 percent while maintaining fraud detection recall for real-time financial risk assessment.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions in the United States face mounting pressure to detect fraud in real time across distributed payment infrastructures operating on resource-constrained edge hardware. Deep learning models deliver strong predictive accuracy but often exceed strict latency budgets at the edge, while lightweight regression systems provide rapid decisions but sacrifice accuracy under nonlinear transaction behaviors. No existing approach effectively bridges the gap between detection accuracy and sub-millisecond latency requirements in edge-deployed financial risk systems.
approach: Uses a U.S. credit card fraud dataset with anonymized PCA features (V1-V28), transaction amount, and temporal ordering for chronological train-validation-test splits.
Constructs a streaming evaluation environment using batch replay to simulate real-time payment authorization cycles with regulated inter-batch delays.
Deploys a deep neural network trained on full feature sets for complex pattern recognition alongside lightweight adaptive regression models (Passive Aggressive, SGD) for rapid online updates.
Implements a hybrid optimization controller that routes transactions based on real-time latency measurements and model confidence thresholds.
Simulates edge hardware constraints including reduced CPU cores and memory budgets to test deployment feasibility.
Applies dynamic quantization to compress the deep student model from 16KB to 8KB while maintaining acceptable latency.
Evaluates predictive performance using PR AUC, recall, precision, and F1 across standalone and hybrid configurations.
Conducts Pareto analysis to map the accuracy-latency trade-off frontier for deployment decision-making.
Performs robustness checks including concept drift simulation, adversarial latency stress testing, and threshold sensitivity analysis.
findings: num: Hybrid routing reduces inference latency by up to 55 percent compared to deep learning alone
num: Deep learning model achieves PR AUC of 0.0009, regression model 0.0008 under default threshold
num: Quantized student model occupies 8253 bytes (8KB) with 0.347ms latency on edge
num: Fast regression model averages 0.31ms latency in edge_tiny simulated environment
num: Median hybrid cascade latency stays at 0.501ms during low fraud activity

key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Class distribution and transaction amount by class → Shows extreme class imbalance with fraud under 1 percent of transactions.
Figure 2: Fraud rate by hour of day and day of week → Slight temporal variations suggest opportunistic fraud timing patterns.
Figure 3: Concept drift and correlation analysis → Fraud behavior evolves gradually, requiring adaptive threshold models.
Figure 4: Rolling fraud incidence analysis → Fraud signals are rare against a stable transaction background.
Figure 5: Predictive Performance metrics → Deep learning achieves marginally higher PR AUC than regression alone.
Figure 6: Latency and Resource Efficiency metrics → Quantized deep model fits 8KB with 0.347ms latency on edge.
Figure 7: Trade-Off Analysis metrics → Cascade routing preserves PR AUC while limiting expensive deep calls.
Figure 8: Robustness Checks metrics → Hybrid system maintains performance under concept drift and latency stress.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper contributes a hybrid optimization framework that dynamically routes financial transactions between deep neural networks and lightweight adaptive regression based on real-time latency and confidence signals. It demonstrates that hybrid routing can reduce inference latency by up to 55 percent compared to standalone deep learning while preserving fraud detection performance under simulated edge hardware constraints. The study introduces a latency-accuracy Pareto analysis methodology for evaluating financial risk systems under operational constraints. It provides empirical evidence that model quantization and dynamic routing make deep learning feasible for resource-constrained edge devices in payment infrastructure. The work establishes a practical blueprint for deploying intelligent fraud detection at the point of transaction.
directly_justifies: Hybrid routing reduces inference latency by up to 55 percent compared to deep learning alone while maintaining fraud detection recall.

topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scanning of all 14 topic domains was conducted. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) was flagged as relevant at contextual level, as the paper reviews existing fraud detection and edge computing approaches in financial systems. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged at low relevance, as the paper applies predictive modeling techniques including deep learning and regression to financial transaction risk assessment, though focused on institutional fraud detection rather than personal finance. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) was flagged at low relevance, since fraud detection is fundamentally an anomaly detection problem in financial data, but the paper addresses institutional payment fraud rather than personal spending anomalies. Domain 9 (Mobile/Edge Design) was flagged at contextual to low relevance, as the paper discusses edge computing and mobile payment device constraints. Domain 10 (Privacy/Trust) was flagged at low relevance, as the paper mentions data privacy benefits of edge processing and trust in automated financial decisions. Domain 14 (ML Serving) was flagged at low relevance, as the paper addresses ML model deployment and on-device inference on resource-constrained hardware. Domains 1 (Filipino Young Professionals), 2 (Filipino Financial Practices), 3 (Expense Categorization), 5 (Behavioral Profiles), 7 (Budgeting Strategies), 11 (Engagement), 12 (Evaluation Frameworks), and 13 (Savings/Debt) were considered and rejected as the paper does not cover personal finance management, budgeting, spending categorization, or user engagement topics. The paper is primarily focused on institutional financial fraud detection at the edge, which falls outside the core personal finance management scope of the Odin topic taxonomy.
